claims.text: The combined containerless experimental and CALPHAD method can accurately and efficiently determine melting temperature across a broad range of HEAs.
The method can determine fusion enthalpy and entropy across a broad range of HEAs.
The method can determine melting-induced volume change and key liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across a broad range of HEAs.
Electromagnetic-levitation DSC can record heating curves and recalescence events without a container.
CALPHAD simulations can predict liquid-solid transition parameters for the studied HEAs.
An inert-gas or vacuum environment avoids contamination and heterogeneous nucleation.
The proposed measurements use heating rates of 10–50 K/min.
Electromagnetic levitation is accessible for HEA melting temperatures up to approximately 2000–2500 °C.
High configurational entropy in HEAs promotes a relatively simple liquid phase without strong short-range-order complications.
Containerless processing minimizes heterogeneous effects and permits intrinsic thermodynamic properties to be captured accurately.
Levitation minimizes contact-induced nucleation and chemical contamination.
Rapid, high-resolution calorimetry precisely captures melting onset and recalescence.
Iterative refinement of CALPHAD models with levitation-calorimetry data enables prediction of fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting-induced volume change.
Integrating containerless calorimetry with CALPHAD reduces uncertainty relative to conventional containerized calorimetry.
The integrated method will yield melting temperatures within ±10 K.
The integrated method will yield fusion enthalpies and entropies with errors below ±5%.
The integrated method will measure volume changes at melting with ±1% relative uncertainty.
Liquid density and viscosity will vary systematically with composition as predicted by CALPHAD.
Conventional container DSC or arc melting can produce melting-temperature uncertainties exceeding ±20 K and larger errors in latent heat and volume change.
The approach is limited to well-homogenized, congruently melting HEAs within the levitation temperature range and excludes alloys that decompose before melting.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator assumes that HEA liquids generally lack strong short-range-order complications, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that variations in liquid short-range order may cause unforeseen deviations.

The advertised errors are ±10 K for melting temperature, below ±5% for fusion quantities, and ±1% for volume change, but the approach is rejected only for deviations greater than ±10%. This allows substantial failure of the stated fusion and volume accuracy targets without satisfying the numerical falsification criterion.
